public_rationale: On January 1, 2025, under 'High confidence', Marcus predicted that AI agents would be endlessly hyped throughout 2025 but far from reliable, except possibly in very narrow use cases. OpenAI promoted agents in January, June, and October 2025, from saying they may 'join the workforce' to launching tools to build them. Independent benchmarks found the best agent completed 30% of simulated workplace tasks (September 2025) and 2.5% of real remote-work projects (30 October 2025).
limitations: The promotion shown comes from one company, OpenAI. It does not measure how much agents were promoted across the industry.
Both benchmarks are preprints, and the latest is from 30 October 2025, not the end of the year.
Whether an agent use counts as a 'very narrow use case' is not defined by the speaker.

except possibly in very narrow use cases
'my own predictions for where we will be at the end of this year', post dated 2025-01-01
our_interpretation: We read 'endlessly hyped' as leading AI companies promoting agents at points spread across 2025, including its last quarter.
We read 'far from reliable' as independent tests from late 2025 showing general-purpose agents failing a large share of realistic multi-step work tasks. Narrow uses are excepted by the speaker.
Evidence from earlier in 2025 is shown too, but the end of the year must be covered.
criteria.support_condition: Leading AI companies promoted agents at points spread across 2025, including its last quarter, and independent tests published late in 2025 show general-purpose agents failing a large share of realistic multi-step work tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent tests published late in 2025 show general-purpose agents completing most realistic multi-step work tasks across broad uses, or agents were not prominently promoted during 2025.

evidence.excerpt: in 2025, we may see the first AI agents “join the workforce” and materially change the output of companies.
evidence.explanation: Early in 2025, OpenAI's CEO said AI agents may 'join the workforce' that year. This shows agents promoted as transformative at the start of 2025. It is a company statement about its own field, not a test of agents.

evidence.excerpt: 2025 has seen the arrival of agents that can do real cognitive work; writing computer code will never be the same.
evidence.locator: Sam Altman, 'The Gentle Singularity', personal blog
evidence.explanation: In June 2025, OpenAI's CEO said 2025 had seen agents that can do real cognitive work. This shows the promotion continuing mid-year. It is a company claim, not an independent test; its example, writing code, is one use.

evidence.excerpt: the most competitive agent can complete 30% of tasks autonomously.
evidence.explanation: An independent benchmark of agents on tasks from a simulated software company, revised in September 2025: the best agent completed 30% of tasks on its own, and harder long-horizon tasks were still beyond reach. Simpler tasks were often solved. This is a preprint.

evidence.excerpt: Today we’re launching AgentKit, a complete set of tools for developers and enterprises to build, deploy, and optimize agents.
evidence.explanation: In October 2025, OpenAI launched a product line for building and deploying agents. This shows agents still being promoted in the last quarter of 2025. It is a company announcement, not a test of agents.

evidence.excerpt: AI agents perform near the floor on RLI, with the highest-performing agent achieving an automation rate of 2.5%.
evidence.explanation: An independent benchmark of real, paid remote-work projects across many sectors, published 30 October 2025. The best agent completed 2.5% of projects to the required standard. This is a preprint.
